# Gate Logic Checklist: Fix Release-Train Detection in cto-review

**Purpose**: Validate that spec.md's requirements for the release-train promote-branch
predicate are complete, unambiguous, consistent, measurable, and cover all decision paths —
before trusting them as the bar for implementation.
**Created**: 2026-09-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `speckit.checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements. It validates the requirements as written, not the implementation.
Checked (`[x]`) = the spec satisfies the question as written. Unchecked (`[ ]`) = a gap, with
a note on whether it is blocking.

## Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the source field for the team-declared promote branch named explicitly (path, owning object)? [Spec §Clarifications — `deploy.production_branch`]
- [x] CHK002 Is the "no team match" outcome specified as its own decision path, distinct from "team match but no field"? [Spec §FR-002, §FR-003 — both collapse to the same unconfigured outcome, which is itself the specified behavior]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the CLI-unreachable case (the team-config source itself failing) addressed as a requirement, not left implicit? [Gap, non-blocking — FR-003 covers "no team declares a promote branch" but an unreachable lookup is a distinct failure mode; implementation treats it the same as unconfigured (fail-open), consistent with FR-004's "every decision...MUST print a rationale"]
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec state what must be recorded when the decision is "unconfigured", not just when it is required/not-required? [Spec §FR-004]

## Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "the repo's matching team entry" in FR-002 unambiguous about what happens if MORE than one team entry matches the same repo? [Gap, non-blocking — not addressed in spec prose; implementation now resolves this explicitly (ambiguous match → unconfigured, distinct status from "no match"), covered by fixture T008c, but the requirement text itself doesn't state it]
- [x] CHK006 Is User Story 2's acceptance criterion free of grammatical ambiguity that could be read two ways? [Spec §User Story 2 — fixed 2026-09-11, was previously malformed]
- [x] CHK007 Is "release-train status" in FR-001 defined precisely enough to distinguish it from "merge authority" (a separate, pre-existing decision covered by `deploy.release_mode`)? [Spec §FR-001, §FR-002]

## Consistency

- [x] CHK008 Do FR-002 and FR-003 agree on what "no team declares a promote branch" means (absent team entry vs. present entry with an absent field)? [Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK009 Are the User Story 1 acceptance scenarios (default branch `develop`) and the Success Criteria (SC-001 says `feature -> develop`) using the base branch consistently? [Spec §User Story 1 Acceptance 1, §SC-001 — consistent intent]

## Measurability

- [ ] CHK010 Can FR-004's "print a rationale" be objectively verified (a specific string/marker), or is "rationale" left to interpretation? [Gap, non-blocking — no required format specified beyond "print" and "record"; implementation settled on a fixed `[cto-review] staging evidence gate: ...` prefix]
- [x] CHK011 Is SC-004's "turns fixtures red" measurable without referring to a specific test file or harness? [Spec §SC-004 — measurable via the existing fixture-harness convention already established for this skill]
- [x] CHK012 Is FR-005's "no company-specific branch literals" measurable via a mechanical check (e.g., grep), or does it require human judgment? [Spec §FR-005]

## Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec cover the case where the resolved promote branch equals the PR's base on a conventional single-branch repo (default branch = promote branch, e.g. `main -> main`)? [Gap, non-blocking — not in User Story 2 acceptance; implementation fixture T011 covers the no-regression case but spec.md doesn't require it]
- [x] CHK014 Does the spec address what "PR" means when there is no PR context available (e.g., predicate run outside a PR review)? [Not applicable — predicate is always invoked with a PR in context per the existing step ordering; out of scope for this fix]
- [x] CHK015 Are both directions of the original bug (false positive AND false negative) each backed by a distinct Success Criterion? [Spec §SC-001 (false positive), §SC-002 (false negative), §SC-003 (third failure mode)]

## Edge Cases

- [ ] CHK016 Is there a requirement for what happens when the team-config lookup returns malformed/unexpected JSON (not just "unreachable")? [Gap, non-blocking — FR-003 covers "no team declares" but not malformed-response handling explicitly; implementation's jq pipeline degrades malformed JSON to the same unconfigured/fail-open outcome via `2>/dev/null || echo ""`]
- [ ] CHK017 Is there a requirement for how an ambiguous repo-to-team mapping (multiple teams claiming the same repo) should resolve, mirroring the existing `resolve-merge-strategy.sh` precedent? [Gap, non-blocking — not stated in spec.md; implementation now gives ambiguity its own explicit `ambiguous` status (distinct from "no match" and "field absent") resolving to `unconfigured`, mirroring `resolve-merge-strategy.sh`'s convention, and is fixture-covered (T008c) — the requirement text itself still doesn't state it]
- [x] CHK018 Does the spec state that the fail-open default must never silently pass without a printed reason (i.e., "unconfigured" must always be distinguishable from "not required because it doesn't match")? [Spec §FR-004]

## Notes

  directly in spec.md.
- The remaining gaps (CHK003, CHK005, CHK010, CHK013, CHK016, CHK017 — **6 items, confirmed by
  recount during the 2026-09-11 correction pass**) are spec-completeness notes, not implementation
  defects: in every case the shipped predicate already resolves the unstated scenario conservatively
